# *** WHAT THEY SETTLE. ***
# 1. ROQUE WAS BORN AT CAPE TOWN, not in Argentina. The family was in the Cape by December 1905,
#    three years before the 1908 enrolment card was filed at the Cape Town office and twenty-three
#    years after Pablo Armando's own birth at Rosario. That was the single question this archive
#    proposed to spend R2,850 answering.
# 2. Roque's death notice names his father as *** ROBERTO LERENA *** - the anglicised "Robert Paul"
#    form, written by his own widow. It ties Pablo Armando and Robert Paul together in a family
#    document rather than a clerk's index.
# 3. NUNO'S DEATH NOTICE NAMES NO PARENTS AT ALL. Item 19 carries the single word "Deceased" and a
#    ditto mark. *** This archive predicted it would name Pablo Armando and Mary Septima. It does
#    not. *** A death notice is only as good as the informant's knowledge, and his widow either did
#    not know her husband's parents' names or did not trouble to write them.
# 4. Neither man followed his father onto the turf: a retired railwayman and a salesman.
# 5. Cheryl Ann Lerena appears as a minor in 1971 - the same woman whose DNA is read on /dna/.
# 6. *** CATHERINE TERTIA *** - "the third". Beside MARY SEPTIMA, "the seventh". The naming habit
#    runs through the Taylor side and out the other end into a granddaughter.
# *** A DISCREPANCY LEFT STANDING. *** data/lerena-register.tsv gives Roque's birth as 25 November
# 1905 from a Corpus Christi Wynberg baptism. The death notice and his identity number both say
# *** 6 December 1905 ***. Eleven days apart. Baptism on the 6th and birth on the 25th of the month
# before is the ordinary shape of it, but this archive has not opened the baptism image to check,
# and the two dates are both recorded rather than one being quietly preferred.
